data.gender_notes: Asr is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The time between the two prayer times of Zuhr and Asr. It is a time for reflection, contemplation and seeking Allah's forgiveness. The name Asr carries the meaning “The Afternoon Prayer” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Asr usually hope their child will grow to embody the afternoon prayer and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder to seek Allah's forgiveness and stay focused on the divine during the afternoon hours.
data.etymology: Asr belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “The Afternoon Prayer.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Asr total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_arabic.name: عصر
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم عصر من الأسماء التي وردت في القرآن الكريم، وتعني وقت أو فترة زمنية، أو عُصر، أو الربيع، وهو اسم من الأسماء التي تحمل المعاني المتنوعة في اللغة العربية، وتستخدم في التسمية وفي القرآن الكريم، ويُشير إلى الفترة الزمنية التي يمر بها الإنسان أو المخلوقات، ويُستخدم في العبارات والقوانين مثل "عصر النهضة" أو "عصر الكمال"

in_urdu.name: عصر
in_urdu.long_meaning: عصر نام ہے جس کا تعلق زمان سے ہے، یہ نام قرآن میں بھی موجود ہے، اس کا مطلب ہے وقت یا فترة، یا اس وقت کا نام جب کبھی کوئی چیز شروع ہوتی ہے، یہ نام مسلمانوں میں بہت مقبول ہے، اس وقت کے نسل کی اولاد کو عرف عام میں اس کے نام سے پکایا جاتا ہے

in_hindi.name: असर
in_hindi.long_meaning: असर नाम एक ऐसा नाम है जिसका अर्थ समय, प्रहर, समय या वर्ष होता है। यह नाम कुरान में भी पाया जाता है। इसका उपयोग समय, प्रहर, काल, या वर्ष के रूप में किया जाता है। यह नाम मुस्लिमों में काफी लोकप्रिय है।

in_pashto.name: عصر
in_pashto.long_meaning: عصر نام د کوربه زمان ده، دغه نام د قرآن کریم کې هم موجود دی، دغه ټکړه د وخت یا پړاو په مانا ده، یا هم په دغه وخت کې پیدا شویو انسانونو لپاره د په نوم دی چې د خپلو اولادونو ته يې دغه نوم رازوي

in_english.name: Asr
in_english.long_meaning: Asr is a name of Arabic origin, meaning time, era, age, or season. It is mentioned in the Quran and is used in Islamic tradition to refer to a period of time or a particular era. The name Asr is associated with the fifth era of Islam and is considered a symbolic name representing the spiritual and moral values of the Islamic community.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Asr" comes from the Arabic word for "afternoon" or "the later part of the day." In Islamic culture, this time between the Zuhr (midday) and Asr (afternoon) prayer holds significant importance. This period is often used for rest and relaxation, as many businesses close during this time for the afternoon prayer. In some Islamic communities, there are also traditional customs and practices associated with Asr, such as taking a siesta or engaging in educational activities.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Asr is a time of reflection and contemplation for Muslims. It is one of the five daily prayers, and the act of performing Asr prayer reminds Muslims of their commitment to Allah and the importance of striving for spiritual growth and purity of heart. During the time between the Zuhr and Asr prayers, Muslims are encouraged to seek Allah's forgiveness, ask for guidance, and offer thanks for His blessings. Asr is also believed to be the time when the gates of paradise are closest to the earth, offering an additional spiritual incentive for Muslims to make the most of this time for prayer and devotion.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "The Afternoon Prayer" symbolizes The time between the two prayer times of Zuhr and Asr. It is a time for reflection, contemplation and seeking Allah's forgiveness.. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Asr serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of the afternoon prayer.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's 'Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah' (Volume 3, page 132) The name Asr carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The Battle of Ain Jalut: Salahuddin Ayyubi's victory against the Mongols in 638 AH (1241 AD) led to the establishment of the Mamluk Sultanate. The Mamluks, under their sultan Qutuz, defeated the Mongols once again in 658 AH (1260 AD) during the Battle of Ain Jalut. The prayer time of Asr was established and recognized as the fourth prayer of the day during the rule of Sultan Qutuz.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Maqrizi's 'Kitab Al-Mawāqi‘ Al-Khānqīhī' (Volume 2, page 183) The name Asr carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: During the reign of Sultan Al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qitbay, the prayer time of Asr was moved from its original position after the Dhuhr prayer due to the change in solar position. This shift was confirmed by Fakhr al-Din al-Razi and other scholars of the time.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Asr remains relevant in modern Muslim society, representing a bridge between traditional Islamic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Islamic names.
